thesis: The Qur'an commands believers to prepare force with full seriousness as deterrence while remaining inwardly free to accept genuine peace, holding both readiness and peace under tawakkul.

flags.quote: wa in janahu li al-salmi fajnah laha. If they incline to peace, then you incline to it.
flags.issue: 8:61 carries a major classical ikhtilaf never acknowledged: Tabari records Qatadah/Ikrimah/al-Hasan/Ibn Zayd holding it MANSUKH by Bara'ah; Jalalayn cites Ibn Abbas for naskh and Mujahid restricting to Banu Qurayzah; Tabari himself rejects naskh ('قول لا دلالة عليه من كتاب ولا سنة') but restricts to ahl al-kitab/jizyah. File asserts a universal standing peace command with no ikhtilaf and no tadabbur-vs-fatwa note, on a war passage quoted adversarially.
Hukm of i'dad stated as flat obligation without fiqh anchor or tadabbur/fatwa line.

notes: Thesis well grounded (Ibn Kathir carries prepare-then-accept-peace via Hudaybiyah; Tabari holds 8:61 muhkam). Fix is additive: short ikhtilaf paragraph (naskh view vs Tabari/Ibn Kathir muhkam, Mujahid's takhsis) + tadabbur-not-fatwa sentence. 23/23 morphology tags verify.

thesis: Believers must answer revelation now as the source of real life because Allah, not the self, controls the heart's openness, and tolerated wrongdoing becomes a communal fitnah that engulfs more than its perpetrators.
notes: All three thesis components verify (Tabari's tarjih on lima yuhyikum; muqallib-al-qulub material; encompassing-fitnah carried by 3 of 4 editions + Ibn Abbas amr-bil-maruf report). File hedges the yahulu mystery appropriately. Reviewer note: 'the verse explicitly says' slightly overstates given the grammarians' ikhtilaf on la tusibanna — below flag threshold. 23/23 morphology tags verify.
